MUTINY ON ONE'S KNEES
In 1908, a faction of Russian thinkers
launched a campaign against dialectical
materialism. They claimed to be
Marxists, yet proudly allied with the
"recent philosopy" of Ernst Mach and
Avenarius, attempting to replace
materialism with "empirio-criticism
Lenin's Diagnosis: This was not a step forward,
but a retreat into reactionary philosophy. A
complete renunciation of Marxism dressed up in
endless subterfuges.

The 1710 Blueprint: Bishop George Berkeley
Color
Scent
The Mechanic: Berkeley argued that we only
perceive "ideas" (qualities like color, taste,
smell, shape). Because these always
occur together, we give them one name.
The Conclusion: Therefore, an apple is
merely a "collection of ideas" or a
"combination of sensations."
Touch
The Rule: Objects do not exist "without the
mind." To claim an invisible, intangible
"matter" sits behind these sensations is a
manifest contradiction.

Concept: David Hume and his
"positivist" followers accept
sensations as the "primary and
irreducible states of consciousness"
but refuse to commit to their origin.
The Stance: They argue we can never
know if perceptions are caused by
external objects, the mind itself, or
an unknown spirit. Experience is
"entirely silent" on the connection.

The Materialist Counter-Model: Diderot's Egg (1769)
Inert Matter / The Egg
The Argument: Diderot
challenged the idealists
by showing how inert
matter becomes
sentient.
Heat / Motion Applied
The Process: From inert
matter organized in a certain
way, impregnated with heat
and motion, consciousness
and sensation are generated.
Sensibility / Life / Memory
The Conclusion: Sensation is
not a barrier to the world, but
a general property of matter in
motion, an evolutionary product
of physical organization.
Noreno

The
"Insane Piano" of Solipsism
Concept:
Diderot noted that humans are like
sentient instruments-our senses are keys
upon which surrounding nature strikes.
The Idealist Trap:
If you adopt Berkeley's view that only
sensations exist, you create a closed
loop, completely cut off from the
external world.
Pull-quote:
«There was a moment of insanity when
the sentient piano imagined that it
was the only piano in the world, and
that the whole harmony of the universe
took place within it."

AVENARIUS AND THE BRAINLESS' PHILOSOPHY
THE ARGUMENT: IN 1875, RICHARD AVENARIUS ARGUED THAT
THE PROPOSITION THAT 'MOTION PRODUCES SENSATION' IN
THE BRAIN IS AN ILLUSION. HE CLAIMED THAT TO BELIEVE THE
BRAIN GENERATES SENSATION REQUIRES BELIEVING IN AN
IMPOSSIBLE CREATVE ACT.
THE CONCLUSION: HE DEDUCED THAT SENSATION MUST EXIST
WITHOUT SUBSTANCE. "WE WE MUST REGARD THE EXISTING
SENSATION, AT THE BASIS OF WHICH THERE IS NOTHING WHICH
DOES NOT POSSESS SENSATION."

European founders have no such
